nodes.title: Read the stored theme defensively
nodes.why: safeReadTheme returns only light or dark and falls back to null when the key is missing, holds another value, or storage access throws, so a blocked or edited store cannot break startup.
nodes.alternative: Read localStorage directly in the constructor and cast whatever string comes back to Theme.
nodes.tradeoff: Storage errors are swallowed without a message, but the toggle keeps working for the session instead of failing to bootstrap.

nodes.title: Hold the theme in a private signal
nodes.why: The service starts from the stored theme, or the in-memory fallback when storage cannot be read, and keeps it in a writable signal that only its own methods change.
nodes.alternative: A public mutable currentTheme field that any component can reassign.
nodes.tradeoff: Components cannot set the value directly and must call setTheme or toggleTheme, which is what keeps storage and the page attribute in step.

nodes.title: Expose the theme as a read-only signal
nodes.why: asReadonly gives components a signal they can read and track but not set, so every change still goes through setTheme and its storage write.
nodes.alternative: Expose the writable signal itself, which lets any component call set and skip persistence and the data-theme update.
nodes.tradeoff: The same value has two names, theme inside the service and currentTheme outside, in exchange for a single write path.

nodes.title: Apply the theme when the service is created
nodes.why: The constructor sets data-theme on the html element as soon as the root component injects the service, so a stored dark theme is in place before that component first renders.
nodes.alternative: Set data-theme in an afterNextRender callback, which runs after the first render and can show the light colors for a frame.
nodes.tradeoff: A constructor with a DOM side effect is less pure, but it is the earliest point the app can act; only a script in index.html could run sooner.

nodes.title: Persist and apply in the same method
nodes.why: setTheme sets the signal, writes storage and updates data-theme in one synchronous call, and toggleTheme goes through it, so the label, the stored key and the page colors cannot drift.
nodes.alternative: An effect that watches the theme signal and writes storage and the attribute whenever it reruns.
nodes.tradeoff: The three steps are written out by hand, but they happen on the click itself, while an effect would also write the default theme to storage on the first visit.

nodes.title: Derive isDark from the service signal
nodes.why: isDark recomputes whenever currentTheme changes, whether this button or any other caller of setTheme changed it, and the OnPush template reads it for both the icon and the label.
nodes.alternative: Copy the theme into a component field on each click, which goes stale when another component switches the theme.
nodes.tradeoff: The template calls isDark() rather than reading a field, a small syntax change for a label that cannot disagree with the service.
